summary.headline: Adani Power Q1 FY27 continuing EBITDA rose 22% to INR6,983 crore and PAT 47% to INR4,867 crore on 78% PLF.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was the company's strongest quarter on a continuing basis, driven by heatwave-led demand, higher PLF (78% vs 67%) and new PPAs for previously merchant capacity at Butibori and Tuticorin. Continuing revenue rose 28% to INR17,550 crore, while fuel cost rose 30% to INR9,513 crore on higher volumes and imported coal indices. Reported figures include a one-time net prior-period revenue recognition of INR1,386 crore linked to revised historic energy charges under certain PPAs. Management reiterated the 45 GW target (revised from 42 GW), an expansion capex of about INR25,000 crore this year, and a net debt-to-EBITDA band of 2-3x, while seeking an enabling resolution for a QIP.

guidance_outlook: Capacity target raised to 45 GW from 42 GW, same timeline (around 2031); 23.7 GW programme unchanged in capex terms.
Expansion capex about INR25,000 crore in FY27, about INR33,000 crore in FY28, and more than INR35,000 crore thereafter; total programme about INR2 lakh crore.
Net debt-to-EBITDA currently slightly above 2x; management expects it to stay between 2x and 3x and not cross 3x.
Korba Phase-II (1,320 MW) expected before December 2026; Mahan Phase-II (1,600 MW) first unit targeted Q1 FY28, second unit about 6 months later, with an attempt to bring it into Q2.
Management expects more stability in revenue and EBITDA as most capacity moves to long-term contracts; 95% of capacity is tied up, 56% of upcoming capacity is under long-term PPAs.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on operations and financials, with firm targets on capex and capacity. Management was guarded or evasive on nuclear timing, which depends on pending government rules, and on the PTSL supply contract, where it declined to give tariff or volume detail.

qa_highlights.question: Will Jaiprakash be consolidated, and what expansion is possible at Bina and Nigri?
qa_highlights.answer: JPVL (24% stake) is an associate; only the share of profit is consolidated, not P&L or balance sheet line by line. Bina and Nigri have large land banks, with Bina also being assessed for nuclear suitability; no expansion planned yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nuclear plan, technology and timing for the 10 GW target by 2035?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is evaluating domestic and foreign technology on per-MW cost, but cannot finalise ordering or investment until government rules under the Act are notified. Sites are being readied and studies are underway; execution would take at least 5 years by its standard.

qa_highlights.question: What is the receivable position from Bangladesh?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables were about USD400 million at end-June 2026, down quarter-on-quarter; about USD100 million is being received monthly, with collections expected slightly above monthly billing.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 3 GW additional capacity being planned and is it under PPA?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a planning-stage buffer for future state bids, since the 24 GW pipeline is tied to specific locations; capex and equipment orders are not firmed up. The 24% JPVL stake (2,220 MW) could be increased.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the strong EBITDA growth when capacity rose only about 4-5%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to higher capacity charges from converted Tuticorin, Raipur and Vidarbha capacity, higher volumes, and higher energy-charge contribution where imported coal indices rose.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex, funding and QIP plans, and has the capex changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR25,000 crore in FY27, INR33,000 crore in FY28 and over INR35,000 crore after; the programme is unchanged. Funding is mainly internal accruals (FFO about INR20,000 crore a year), with interim gaps of about INR60,000 crore from debt. The QIP is an enabling EGM resolution with no timeline or dilution detail yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt-to-EBITDA outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt-to-EBITDA is slightly above 2x, and management expects it to stay between 2x and 3x and never cross 3x.

qa_highlights.question: Will dividends or bonuses be paid given large reserves?
qa_highlights.answer: No; surplus is being reinvested in the capex programme over the next 6-7 years, as management believes return on capital exceeds the dividend payout benefit.

capex_capacity: Expansion capex guided at about INR25,000 crore in FY27, about INR33,000 crore in FY28 and more than INR35,000 crore thereafter; total programme of more than INR2 lakh crore, with no change to the capex programme per CFO.

Target raised to 45 GW from 42 GW, same timeline (around 2031); management said the 23.7 GW programme is unchanged. Additional ~3 GW being planned for future state bids, at planning stage with no firm capex or equipment order.

Korba Phase-II (1,320 MW) expected before December 2026; Mahan Phase-II (1,600 MW) first unit in Q1 FY28, second unit about 6 months later, with an attempt to bring it into Q2. Raipur Phase-II and Raigarh Phase-II are over 62% and 54% complete; Mirzapur 1,600 MW greenfield execution has started. All 24 GW of BTG has been ordered.

Jaiprakash 180 MW Churk plant acquired under insolvency; not operational, expected to take about 6 months to revive, not tied to any PPA, and little contribution expected in the current year. 24% stake in JPVL is accounted as an associate (share of profit only).

Nuclear: about 10 GW target by 2035 (raised from 5 GW); ordering and capital allocation await government rules under the Act. Management said execution should take at least 5 years by its standards. Bina and Nigri have land banks for thermal or nuclear.
Hydro: 570 MW Bhutan project; PPA and tariff structure not yet finalised. Plant-level FFO of about INR20,000 crore per year cited for funding the capex plan.
demand_pricing: Peak demand hit a record of about 271 GW in May 2026; national energy consumption rose 8.4% YoY to 485 billion units in Q1 FY27 on heatwaves.

PPA tariff realisation rose 8% YoY to INR5.93/unit, including fixed capacity charges on newly contracted Butibori (600 MW) and Tuticorin (600 MW) capacity; merchant and short-term realisation rose 13% to INR7.04/unit.
PPA sales grew 30% to 25 billion units; merchant volumes fell to 4 billion units from 6 billion units as capacity moved to PPAs. Some Raipur capacity is also now under a PPA with Karnataka.

Fuel cost rose 30% to INR9,513 crore on higher dispatch and higher imported coal indices; management attributed about INR2,200 crore EBITDA gain to fuel cost change, reflecting volume, indexed variable tariffs and merchant prices.

Tied-up capacity is about 95%, with most on long-term contracts; 56% of upcoming capacity is under long-term PPAs. Bids pending: UP 4,000 MW, Gujarat 4,000 MW, Uttarakhand 1,320 MW and West Bengal about 3,800 MW (about 13 GW). Untied capacity cited at 11.1 GW in analyst question, with historic bid win rate of about two-thirds.

Bangladesh (Godda): receivables about USD400 million at end-June 2026, with about USD100 million monthly collections from BPDB. Revenue recognised only on undisputed amounts. Godda Q1 generation 2.519 billion units vs 2.362 billion units; revenue INR2,473 crore vs INR2,135 crore.

MSEDCL 2,500 MW supply contract (via PTSL, RE-RTC, minimum 51% green sources): management declined to give tariff or volume detail and said it runs as a trading platform; a 540 MW thermal capacity PPA with Maharashtra will be restructured as a capacity-charge PPA once signed with PTSL.
risks_watch: Execution: Korba Phase-II timing (before December 2026) and Mahan Phase-II unit 1 (Q1 FY28) with possible slippage to Q3 for unit 2; Jaiprakash Churk 180 MW revival expected to take about 6 months.

Bid conversion: about 13 GW of pending state bids and 11.1 GW untied capacity; historic win rate about two-thirds; Korba Phase-II output is unsigned and may sell merchant for a year or two even if a PPA is signed.
Nuclear policy dependency: timing, technology and capital allocation remain contingent on government rules under the Act, which management said have been pending for about 6 months.
Funding and leverage: capex of over INR2 lakh crore with about INR60,000 crore debt needed; QIP enabling resolution sought with no size or timeline; watch net debt-to-EBITDA versus the 3x ceiling.
Bangladesh receivables (about USD400 million) and collection pace versus monthly billing; revenue recognised only on undisputed amounts.
Fuel and merchant exposure: higher imported coal indices lifted fuel cost 30%; the MSEDCL/PTSL supply contract and Bhutan 570 MW PPA terms remain undisclosed.
